list_title: The Jacobian conjecture
proposed_open_statement: The Jacobian conjecture in dimension two: a polynomial map F: C^2 -> C^2 with constant nonzero Jacobian determinant is invertible.
basis: Counterexample in dimension three reported (Alpoge; arXiv 2609.17795, 2610.24889; 2611.03572 treats N >= 3 as settled). Not checked here; row restated to the case all reports leave open.

list_title: Kaplansky's zero-divisor conjecture
proposed_open_statement: Kaplansky's zero-divisor conjecture in characteristic zero: for a torsion-free group G and a field K of characteristic 0, the group ring K[G] has no zero divisors.
basis: Reported false in every positive characteristic (p = 2 construction credited to OpenAI; odd p arXiv 2610.17662, 2611.04599). Not checked here.

list_title: Fuglede's conjecture in dimensions one and two
proposed_open_statement: Fuglede's conjecture in dimension one: a bounded measurable set of positive measure in R tiles R by translations if and only if it is spectral.
basis: arXiv 2607.15632 claims both directions fail in R^2 (finite sets in Z_60 x Z_12 lifted to unions of unit squares). The finite sets were checked by us; the transfer to R^2 (its Proposition 2.1 and the cited transfer results) was NOT checked, so dimension two should be marked "claimed refuted, one preprint" rather than settled. Three intervals in dimension one done (2607.24005).

list_title: The Caratheodory conjecture
proposed_open_statement: The Caratheodory conjecture for real-analytic surfaces: every real-analytic closed convex surface in R^3 has at least two umbilic points.
basis: Smooth counterexamples reported (Alpoge; arXiv 2610.34036, a strictly convex closed C-infinity surface with exactly one umbilic). Not checked here.

list_title: The MDS conjecture
proposed_open_statement: The linear MDS conjecture for odd non-prime q: a linear MDS code of dimension k over F_q, q = p^h with p odd and h >= 2, has length at most q + 1 (q + 2 in the two known exceptional cases), outside the range already proved.
basis: Prime q is Ball's theorem; even characteristic claimed in arXiv 2610.28208 (one preprint); linear-in-q range of dimensions known (2610.03740).

list_title: Vaught's conjecture
proposed_open_statement: Vaught's conjecture for first-order theories: a complete first-order theory in a countable language has either countably many or 2^aleph_0 countable models up to isomorphism.
basis: arXiv 2610.15217 gives a Lean-verified counterexample for L_{omega_1,omega}. Not checked here.

list_title: The final state conjecture and stability of Kerr for all subextremal angular momenta
proposed_open_statement: The final state conjecture: generic asymptotically flat vacuum initial data evolve into a finite number of Kerr black holes moving apart, plus radiation.
basis: Nonlinear stability of Kerr in the full subextremal range announced in arXiv 2606.28253 (Hintz, one preprint, not confirmed); the stability part should be marked "announced" until refereed.

list_title: The Atiyah conjecture on L^2 Betti numbers
proposed_open_statement: The Atiyah conjecture for torsion-free groups: for a torsion-free group G, every L^2 Betti number of a finite free G-CW complex (equivalently, the von Neumann rank of every matrix over Q[G]) is an integer.
basis: The rationality form is false (Austin; Grabowski). Partial results: strong Atiyah for finite-index torsion-free subgroups of Out of surface, free and right-angled Artin groups (arXiv 2606.19606).

list_title: Gaussian free field limit of the six-vertex height function
proposed_open_statement: Gaussian free field limit of the six-vertex height function for the remaining range of Delta in [-1, 1/2) not covered by arXiv 2603.06268 (-1 <= Delta <= -1/2, full plane) and arXiv 2610.07454 (Dirichlet boundary, simply connected domains, a range including Delta near 0).
basis: As in DESERVE.tsv; the exact endpoints of the 2610.07454 range should be copied from that paper before the row is edited.

list_title: The density conjecture for activated random walk
proposed_open_statement: The density conjecture for activated random walk in dimension two and higher: the driven-dissipative stationary density equals the fixed-energy critical density.
basis: Dimension one proved (arXiv 2502.02579; 2605.00207).

list_title: Gaussian free field fluctuations of lozenge tilings of general domains (Kenyon–Okounkov)
proposed_open_statement: Gaussian free field fluctuations for lozenge tilings of domains outside the class settled by arXiv 2609.04789: non-polygonal boundaries, domains with several liquid components, and multiply connected domains.
basis: Simply connected polygonal domains with one liquid region proved in arXiv 2609.04789 (Huang).

list_title: Mixing time of the lozenge-tiling Glauber dynamics on domains with frozen regions
proposed_open_statement: Mixing time N^{2+o(1)} for the lozenge-tiling Glauber dynamics on general simply connected domains whose limit shape has frozen regions.
basis: The hexagon done in arXiv 2605.26664 (Aggarwal, Toninelli).

list_title: Quantitative Tensor Programs: finite-width rates for any architecture
proposed_open_statement: Quantitative Tensor Programs along training: finite-width rates between a trained network and its infinite-width limit in the feature-learning parametrisation, and the optimal order of the rate.
basis: At initialisation, Wasserstein bounds of order width^(-1/2) for Tensor Programs are given in arXiv 2607.06290.

list_title: Exponential convergence of mean-field SVGD and the Stein log-Sobolev inequality
proposed_open_statement: The Stein log-Sobolev inequality, hence exponential convergence of mean-field SVGD, for kernels outside the class of arXiv 2412.10295 (kernels whose Fourier transform has quadratic decay at infinity), the Gaussian kernel among them.
basis: As in DESERVE.tsv.

list_title: Random planar maps embedded conformally converge to Liouville quantum gravity
proposed_open_statement: Convergence to Liouville quantum gravity of conformally embedded random planar maps for models other than the mated-CRT map and spanning-tree-weighted maps, uniform planar maps (sqrt(8/3)-LQG) under circle packing or Tutte embedding first among them.
basis: arXiv 2610.10480 and 2610.10505 (Holden, Yu) settle the mated-CRT and spanning-tree-weighted models under circle packing and uniformization.

list_title: The Fyodorov–Hiary–Keating conjecture
proposed_open_statement: The limiting law in the Fyodorov–Hiary–Keating conjecture: max over |h| <= 1 of log|zeta(1/2 + i(tau + h))| - log log T + (3/4) log log log T converges in distribution, for tau uniform in [T, 2T], to the law predicted by Fyodorov, Hiary and Keating.
basis: First two orders and tightness of the recentred maximum are in Arguin, Bourgade, Radziwill (parts I and II); the limit law is open.

list_title: The singularity probability of random symmetric sign matrices
proposed_open_statement: The sharp singularity rate for random symmetric sign matrices: P(det M_n = 0) = (1/2 + o(1))^n, the probability that two rows or columns are equal up to sign.
basis: Exponential smallness proved in arXiv 2203.06141 (Campos, Jenssen, Michelen, Sahasrabudhe).

list_title: The capacity region of the general two-receiver broadcast channel
proposed_open_statement: The capacity region of the general two-receiver discrete memoryless broadcast channel (move to the general list).
basis: arXiv 2608.19869 claims Marton's inner bound is strictly suboptimal for some channels (one preprint, not confirmed); if confirmed, the tightness question is answered and only the region itself stays open.

list_title: Uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for noiseless training of two-layer networks
proposed_open_statement: The optimal rate, uniform in time, at which the N-particle noiseless gradient flow of a two-layer network approaches its mean-field limit, measured from a quantized initial law (the W2 bound at time zero is limited by the quantization error).
basis: As in DESERVE.tsv (an agent).

list_title: Width needed for gradient descent on deep linear networks from random initialization
proposed_open_statement: Convergence of gradient descent on depth-L linear networks from Gaussian initialization when the width m is of order L (m ~ cL): does it converge with high probability, and for which c?
basis: Depth-independent width answered in the negative (2020); arXiv 2502.02531.

list_title: The smallest eigenvalue of the neural tangent kernel Gram matrix
proposed_open_statement: The sharp constant in the smallest eigenvalue of the neural tangent kernel Gram matrix at minimal overparametrisation, removing the logarithmic factors in the width bounds.
basis: Minimal width answered up to logarithms (arXiv 2205.10217, 2007.12826).

list_title: Random-features regression beyond linear scaling
proposed_open_statement: Remove at the next pass unless a case outside arXiv 2403.08160 is named (sharp random-features asymptotics for all polynomial scalings of features, samples and dimension).
basis: As in DESERVE.tsv (an agent).

list_title: Neural collapse under gradient training of an actual network
proposed_open_statement: Neural collapse under gradient training of deep networks (depth >= 3) on general, not orthogonally separable, data, and under discrete-step gradient descent or SGD.
basis: Two-layer ReLU under gradient flow on orthogonally separable data proved in arXiv 2510.21078.

list_title: Does the overlap gap property imply algorithmic hardness?
proposed_open_statement: In random optimisation problems from statistical physics (spin glasses, random constraint satisfaction, perceptrons), does the multi-overlap gap property above a threshold rule out every polynomial-time algorithm there, not only stable or low-degree ones?
basis: OGP alone does not imply hardness: shortest path has it and is easy (arXiv 2411.01836); stable algorithms fail on isolated perceptron solutions (arXiv 2604.00328).

list_title: Efficient learning of one-hidden-layer ReLU networks under Gaussian inputs
proposed_open_statement: The optimal dependence on k of the running time for learning a sum of k ReLUs under Gaussian inputs, e.g. whether poly(d, 1/eps) * f(k) is achievable or the exponent of d must grow with k.
basis: Polynomial time for constant k proved in arXiv 2304.10524.

list_title: Does Metropolized Hamiltonian Monte Carlo mix in d^{1/4} steps?
proposed_open_statement: Mixing of Metropolized HMC in d^{1/4} steps (up to logarithms) for general smooth strongly log-concave targets, without the Frobenius-Lipschitz Hessian condition or without a warm start.
basis: Answered under a Frobenius-Lipschitz Hessian with a warm start in arXiv 2304.04724.

list_title: A polynomial finite-particle rate for Stein variational gradient descent
proposed_open_statement: A polynomial rate in N, uniform in time, for the N-particle SVGD empirical measure (not its time average) to approach the target in Wasserstein distance.
basis: N^(-1/2) in kernel Stein discrepancy for the time-averaged measure is in arXiv 2409.08469; uniform-in-time propagation of chaos with logarithmic rates in arXiv 2607.00149.

list_title: The scaling limit of trained deep residual networks
proposed_open_statement: Scaling limits of trained deep residual networks beyond two-layer blocks (attention or deeper blocks), on time horizons growing with the size, and with sharp error rates.
basis: Two-layer blocks with error O(1/L + sqrt(D/(LM)) + 1/sqrt(D)) are in arXiv 2603.18168.

list_title: Neural scaling laws for nonlinear trained networks
proposed_open_statement: Proof of power-law scaling of the test loss in data, parameters and compute for trained nonlinear networks of general architecture (beyond the single-index and random-feature models).
basis: The row's example is proved in arXiv 2504.19983.

list_title: Emergence of skills from random skill graphs
proposed_open_statement: Emergence of skills in trained nonlinear networks on random skill-graph data beyond the single-index example: does loss decrease in sharp, ordered skill-acquisition steps for multi-index or deep models?
basis: Single-index example proved in arXiv 2504.19983; see also 2410.01243, 2404.07009.

list_title: A theory of weak-to-strong generalization
proposed_open_statement: Weak-to-strong generalisation in the feature-learning regime: conditions under which a strong student trained by gradient descent on a weak teacher's labels exceeds the teacher's accuracy.
basis: Linear models (arXiv 2605.05742) and random-features students (arXiv 2503.02877, 2610.09044) done.

list_title: Convergence of discrete diffusion models
proposed_open_statement: Sharp, vocabulary-size-free convergence rates in KL divergence for discrete diffusion models with general (not only masked or uniform) noising processes, under minimal assumptions on the score error.
basis: IPM bounds free of vocabulary size for masked and uniform priors (arXiv 2605.17232); minimax optimality under sparsity (arXiv 2610.19020). Endpoints to be checked against both papers.

list_title: Offline reinforcement learning with function approximation: what coverage is needed?
proposed_open_statement: The weakest coverage condition, beyond single-policy concentrability with Q*-realizability and Bellman completeness, that suffices for sample-efficient offline RL with general function approximation under partial coverage.
basis: arXiv 2602.12107: Q*-realizability plus Bellman completeness is not enough under partial coverage (information-theoretic lower bound).

list_title: The Hopf-Chern-Thurston sign conjecture
proposed_open_statement: The sign conjecture for nonpositive curvature: a closed Riemannian 2n-manifold of nonpositive sectional curvature has (-1)^n chi >= 0 (and the Chern-Thurston form for closed aspherical 2n-manifolds). Keep the positive-curvature case as "claimed refuted, one preprint, unchecked".
basis: arXiv 2609.11980 (abstract read 13 Nov) claims a smooth metric of strictly positive sectional curvature on S^3 x S^3, found by an automated research agent; no independent check named. Strong prior against: it would be the first new simply connected example in its class in decades. Do not mark settled until a referee or an independent curvature check exists.

list_title: The Pompeiu problem and Schiffer's conjecture
proposed_open_statement: Keep the row, marked "claimed refuted in every dimension 2-21 and infinitely many others (preprints by one author, computer-assisted)"; open remainder if the claims hold: the dimensions not covered, and whether the planar case has a fully machine-checked proof (its verifier ends in numerical gates with analytic lemmas in the text).
basis: arXiv 2609.35419 v2 and the repo github.com/aster2024/schiffer-pompeiu-counterexamples (dimension-19/, infinitely-many-dimensions/). We replayed the n = 8, 10, 14 certificates on 13 Nov: PROVED, PROVED_CONVEX, fail-closed tests pass (PD15_SCHIFFER_REPLAY_1113.txt). A replay on a second platform, not an independent proof.

list_title: Robbins' problem: minimising the expected rank with full information
proposed_open_statement: Determine the limiting value V = lim V(n) of Robbins' full-information expected-rank stopping problem for n i.i.d. uniform observations (known 1.908 <= V <= 2.3262), and decide whether V is attained by a memoryless threshold rule.
basis: arXiv 1606.03348 (rank-plus-threshold rule, expected rank 2.32614, the best upper bound); 2608.27419 (finite MDP abstractions, exact values for small n, no new limiting bound in the abstract). Lower bound 1.908 is Bruss-Ferguson (1993), from our own reading, not re-checked here.

list_title: Sylvester's problem in dimension three and higher
proposed_open_statement: Sylvester's four-point problem in R^d, d >= 3: which convex body K maximises the probability that d+2 independent uniform points of K are not in convex position (conjecture: the simplex)? Ellipsoids are the minimisers in every dimension (Groemer); the maximiser is known only in the plane (Blaschke, the triangle).
basis: arXiv search 13 Nov (Sylvester four-point): only variants (ball-convex bodies 2608.29975, planar segment angles 2609.36517, Gaussian version 2407.02589); nothing on the d >= 3 maximiser. Keep at score 3: a classic, narrow reach.

list_title: Phase transition of the noisy majority vote process on Z^2
proposed_open_statement: For the noisy majority vote process on Z^2 (each site adopts the majority of itself and its four neighbours, flipped with probability epsilon), are there at least two invariant measures for all small epsilon > 0?
basis: Non-ergodicity is now proved on regular trees of degree >= 3 (arXiv 2501.16202, extending Bramson-Gray 2021 for d >= 5) and on nonamenable expanders (2508.06935); Z^2 and Z^d remain open. Statement unchanged; add these as the frontier.

list_title: Rapid mixing of Glauber dynamics for the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model up to β = 1
proposed_open_statement: Rapid (polynomial) mixing of single-site Glauber dynamics for the SK model, with high probability over the disorder, for every beta in (1/2 + epsilon, 1), up to the replica-symmetric threshold beta = 1.
basis: Preprints: optimal O(n log n) mixing for beta < 1/2 (arXiv 2608.22159), a rank-one trickledown extension to beta <= 1/2 + epsilon (2609.13138); simulated annealing samples for beta < 1 (2610.17717, a different statement). Older published range beta < 1/4 then about 0.295. Restate to the gap (1/2 + epsilon, 1).

list_title: Closed orbits in the Lorentz mirror model
proposed_open_statement: In the Lorentz mirror model on Z^2 where each site carries a two-sided mirror with probability q in (0,1] (orientation NE or NW with probability 1/2 each, independently), is every light trajectory almost surely periodic (closed)? Known only for q = 1, where the model is critical bond percolation.
basis: arXiv 2610.12460 (plane graphs with infinite trajectories, each infinite ray has infinitely many pivots, after Quas), 2609.14949 (numerics), 2510.24091 (multiscale conductivity in d dimensions, unit density), 2602.07988 (hierarchical version). None settles the Z^2 question for q < 1.

list_title: Oliveira's conjecture on the mixing time of the interchange process
proposed_open_statement: Oliveira's conjecture: on every finite graph with arbitrary edge rates, the total-variation mixing time of the interchange process is at most a universal constant times that of a single random walk. Alon (arXiv 2610.22151) reduces the remaining cases to comparing the minimal eigenvalues of interchange Laplacians on two Specht modules and conjectures the constant 2/3 (his Conjecture 1.5).
basis: Known: hypercube and high-dimensional products (Hermon-Salez 1905.02146), few-particle comparison (2105.13486), Alon's inverse-polynomial lower bound in the comparable cases (2610.22151). Our own partial work on Conjecture 1.5 (disconnected D = 2 cases with components of at most five vertices, Codex STRAT runs with our exact replays) is unrefereed and does not settle the statement.

list_title: The upper tail problem for subgraph counts (the 'infamous upper tail')
proposed_open_statement: For every fixed graph H and every p = p(n) -> 0 with E X_H -> infinity, determine log P(X_H >= (1+delta) E X_H) up to a factor 1+o(1) in G(n,p). Settled for cliques and regular H in most of the range (Harel-Mousset-Samotij), for stars at every such p (arXiv 2501.03404), and for irregular H when n^{-1/Delta} << p << 1 (2503.05311); open for irregular H below n^{-1/Delta}, where Delta is the maximum degree of H.
basis: Abstracts read 13 Nov: 2610.31590 (random regular graphs), 2503.05311, 2501.03404, 2405.01980 (directed). Restate to the irregular, sparse remainder.

list_title: Is the free Ising measure on a regular tree a factor of IID up to reconstruction?
proposed_open_statement: Is the free-boundary ferromagnetic Ising measure on the d-regular tree a factor of IID for every beta with (d-1)^{-1} < tanh beta <= (d-1)^{-1/2}, i.e. all the way to the reconstruction threshold? It is a factor of IID in uniqueness and is not one beyond reconstruction; Nam-Sly-Zhang construct factors of IID for part of the window between.
basis: arXiv 2012.09484 (Nam, Sly, Zhang); no later abstract found on 13 Nov settling the full window. Statement unchanged; name the window explicitly.

list_title: Optimal rates in the Gaussian-process limit of wide random networks
proposed_open_statement: For a depth-L network with widths n, iid N(0, C_W/fan-in) weights and a Lipschitz activation, viewed as a random field on a compact K in R^d, determine the sharp rate of convergence to the neural-network Gaussian process in a functional metric on C(K) (for instance W_2 on C(K)), with its dependence on the depth L. Rates of order n^{-1/2} in Wasserstein distance and of order 1/n for smooth test functions are known; the sharp functional rate and its depth dependence are not.
basis: arXiv 2607.06290 (Agazzi, Mosig Garcia, Trevisan: tensor programs), 2601.21539 (Celli), 2605.02771 (Giovagnini, Kotitsas, Romito: general weights); Favaro, Hanin, Marinucci, Nourdin, Peccati (order 1/n for smooth test functions). Abstracts read 11 Nov.

list_title: The law of input-output Jacobians of deep random networks with general activations
proposed_open_statement: For a deep network with Gaussian weights and a smooth activation (tanh, GELU) initialised at criticality, prove that the squared Jacobian norm |J u|^2 for a fixed unit input direction u is asymptotically log-normal, with log-variance proportional to sum_l 1/n_l, as Hanin and Nica prove for ReLU with He initialisation. The difficulty is that the derivative matrices depend on weights already used, so the layer increments are not independent. The singular-value law in the joint limit L/n -> t is left to T247.
basis: Hanin, Nica, Products of many large random matrices and gradients in deep neural networks (arXiv 1812.05994; identifier from memory, not re-checked 13 Nov). Split agreed in STATEMENT_PASS 11 Nov.

list_title: Depth-independent sample complexity under spectral-norm constraints
proposed_open_statement: Vardi, Shamir and Srebro show that for one-hidden-layer networks with bounded inputs, spectral-norm control alone does not give width-independent uniform convergence for general Lipschitz activations, but does for sufficiently smooth ones. Open: for smooth activations, is the sample complexity of depth-L networks with ||W_l|| <= M_l bounded in terms of prod M_l alone, independently of depth and width; and does ReLU fall on the negative side? (Absorbs T373.)
basis: arXiv 2202.06233 (Vardi, Shamir, Srebro), abstract read 11 Nov; whether their negative construction covers ReLU not yet checked.

list_title: The curse of parametric complexity in operator learning
proposed_open_statement: For operators past the reach of holomorphy, namely the Hamilton-Jacobi solution operator beyond the caustic time or the entropy-solution operator of a scalar hyperbolic conservation law, do neural operators reach error eps with parameter count and sample size polynomial in 1/eps, with a matching lower bound? Holomorphic operators are settled with optimal sample complexity (Adcock-Dexter-Moraga), and HJ-Net beats the curse for Hamilton-Jacobi before caustics (Lanthaler-Stuart).
basis: arXiv 2406.13928 (Adcock, Dexter, Moraga), 2306.15924 (Lanthaler, Stuart), 2112.08125 (Marcati, Schwab), 2307.09835 (Schwab, Stein, Zech), 2406.18794 (Lanthaler, lower bounds). From the row dossier, 11 Nov.

list_title: Sample-efficient reinforcement learning with linearly realizable optimal value functions
proposed_open_statement: In a finite-horizon MDP with stochastic transitions and a constant number of actions, where only Q* is linear in known d-dimensional features (q*-realizability), is there a planner with a generative model, or an online learner, whose query complexity is polynomial in d and H? Polynomially many actions already force exponential query complexity, a constant suboptimality gap does not help online, and TensorPlan is polynomial for a fixed number of actions under v*-realizability.
basis: Weisz, Amortila, Szepesvari (exponential lower bound, large action sets); arXiv 2110.02195v2 (Weisz, Szepesvari, Gyorgy, few actions); TensorPlan (Weisz et al. 2021). From the row dossier and STATEMENT_PASS, 11 Nov.

list_title: The sample-complexity gain from invariance
proposed_open_statement: For a neural network trained by gradient descent on a target invariant under a group G acting on the input space (a finite group, or a compact Lie group acting smoothly on a compact manifold), prove a sample-complexity gain matching the kernel ridge regression minimax gain: the sample size multiplied by |G| for finite G, and the dimension reduced to that of the quotient for a positive-dimensional G.
basis: Tahmasebi, Jegelka 2023, exact gain for kernel ridge regression including continuous groups (arXiv 2303.14269; identifier from memory, not re-checked 13 Nov). The network case is open.

list_title: Is deep learning a renormalization group flow?
proposed_open_statement: For the critical two-dimensional Ising model on the L x L torus, does representing its distribution to relative-entropy accuracy eps L^2 with a bounded-depth network require exponentially more parameters in L than with depth of order log L? This is the depth-separation half of the renormalization-group analogy; the other half (trained layers implementing a coarse-graining) is left aside.
basis: Mehta, Schwab, An exact mapping between the variational renormalization group and deep learning (arXiv 1410.3831; identifier from memory). The row's own two claims; this restatement keeps the one closest to a theorem.

list_title: Global regularity in three dimensions for defocusing energy-supercritical wave and Schroedinger equations
proposed_open_statement: Prove or disprove that smooth compactly supported data give global smooth solutions for the defocusing wave equation u_tt - Laplacian u + |u|^(p-1) u = 0 on R^(1+3) for odd p >= 7, and for the defocusing Schroedinger equation i u_t + Laplacian u = |u|^(p-1) u on R^(1+3) for odd p with 7 <= p <= 25. Blow-up from smooth data is known for the Schroedinger equation at (d, p) = (3, 27), (4, 9), (5, 7) and for the real wave equation at p = 3, d >= 9; p = 5, d >= 7; p = 7, d >= 6; none of these covers the cases stated.
basis: arXiv 2609.23685 (Buck, Carballeira, Gomez-Serrano, Shi; computer-assisted), 2610.06678v3 (Cadiot, Ionescu, Palasek); abstracts read 11 Nov (GENERAL_LITCHECK). The open range is what those two abstracts leave; other constructions were not searched for on 13 Nov.
